recommendation: Keep the commit as-is; it narrowly fixes invalid implementer-facing example URI strings without changing the accepted work-group guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-19432 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification PA issue asking whether commercial plan and group numbers belong in InsurancePlan.identifier and requesting examples; the final resolution selected post-refactor InsurancePlan.identifier for both plan and group IDs and directed definition/comment updates.
initial_application: Git commit 1b597e8ee07c2c0df02ae2ab2483daddcf1ba808 applied the substantive change by adding the plan/group definition and example comment to source/insuranceplan/structuredefinition-InsurancePlan.xml, but three example Identifier.system URI strings were imported with spaces inside the URI.
additional_context: InsurancePlan is active in source/fhir.ini and owned by PA. FHIR-24827 explains the InsuranceProduct/InsurancePlan refactor that made post-refactor InsurancePlan.identifier the right target, while FHIR-24641 is separate Coverage.class context for patient-specific coverage details. Confluence and Zulip checks found no contrary community record.
reconciliation: Updated source/insuranceplan/structuredefinition-InsurancePlan.xml to remove embedded spaces from the plan/group example Identifier.system URI strings, producing valid https://insurance-payer.com/plan-numbers and https://insurance-payer.com/group-numbers examples.
source_changes: source/insuranceplan/structuredefinition-InsurancePlan.xml: corrected three InsurancePlan.identifier comment example Identifier.system URI values by removing spaces inside the https://insurance-payer.com/... strings.

related_jiras.note: The InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct refactor established the post-refactor target for this identifier guidance; it was background only for this seed decision.

The Coverage.class issue cited in the FHIR-19432 resolution concerns patient-specific coverage identifiers and was already separately audited; it does not supersede the InsurancePlan publication use case.
